title: Contextual signal annotator and alert harmonizer for usage/cost/latency telemetry
creator: Liam Ortega
description:
Problem: The Console is currently generating high-volume, noisy alerts for usage/cost/latency anomalies. Many alerts are duplicates across metrics and tenant slices (e.g., single customer causing correlated spikes in token cost, request latency, and error rates). This increases oncall fatigue and slows incident triage.

Goal: Build a backend service that (1) enriches raw anomaly signals with contextual annotations (recent deploys, model variant, capacity tier, billing plan, rollout tags), (2) groups/ harmonizes correlated alerts into a single coherent incident with a composite severity score, and (3) routes/filters alerts according to customer impact and runbook mappings.

Scope: Service will sit in the telemetry pipeline after anomaly scorers (existing detectors produce candidate signals). It will be responsible for enrichment, correlation heuristics, deduplication, and severity scoring. Initial release focuses on usage/cost/latency signals; later phases expand to model quality and embeddings churn.

Non-goals: Replacing anomaly detection models in this ticket. We will not train new ML detectors yet; this ticket focuses on deterministic, explainable enrichment and grouping logic and the plumbing to enable later ML-based grouping.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment: For 95% of incoming candidate signals, service attaches at least three contextual annotations (deploy-id, model-variant, customer-plan) within 2s of ingestion.
Grouping: Duplicate/redundant alerts reduced by >=40% for internal telemetry over a 14-day A/B run compared to baseline.
Severity scoring: Composite severity correlates with incident impact: top 10 scored incidents should contain >=80% of high-impact incidents in the baseline period.
Routing: Alerts are routed to correct Slack channel or PagerDuty escalation policy based on routing rules for 100% of test tenants in the canary cohort.
Observability: Console dashboard surfaces grouped incidents with links to raw signals, and runbook suggestions are present for >=90% of grouped incidents.
Performance: Added per-signal latency is <50ms p50 and <500ms p99 for enrichment and grouping logic.
Feature flags: Entire service can be toggled per-tenant and per-region for controlled rollout.
tasks: Design API between anomaly detectors and annotator (events + metadata contract)
Implement enrichment connectors (deployments service, model catalog, billing labels) with caching and backpressure handling
Build grouping heuristics engine (time window + tenant affinity + signal similarity) and simple deterministic scoring
Add routing layer with rule engine to map scores to channels/escalation policies
Create observability dashboard: grouped-incident view, dedup metrics, false-positive metrics
Integration tests with synthetic spike generator and e2e canary test harness
Run 14-day internal A/B test and analyze results, iterate on heuristics
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive grouping may hide distinct incidents. Mitigation: conservative default heuristics and expose raw signals in grouped incident view for easy split/inspect.

Risk: Enrichment service depends on churny external metadata (deploys, tags) that may be delayed. Mitigation: use short-lived cache with background refresh and fall back to last-known-good tags with TTL labeling.
Risk: Increased pipeline latency. Mitigation: instrument p50/p95/p99 and early abort path to emit minimal alert if enrichment times out; mark incident as partially-enriched.
Risk: Routing misclassification affecting customers. Mitigation: start with internal-only routing, then a small customer canary with manual review and signoff.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal Alpha): enable for internal telemetry and developer orgs only (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5 low-risk customers with feature flag; monitor false positives and routing correctness (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta): expand to 25% of customers; run A/B comparison for dedup reduction and MTTD impact (14 days)
Phase 3 (GA): opt-in for all customers; enable default grouping with customer override and UI toggle
test_plan: Unit tests for enrichment connectors with mocked metadata stores
Integration test against streaming pipeline using local kafka fixtures
Synthetic spike generator to validate grouping heuristics for correlated multi-metric incidents
Canary e2e with 5 tenants and manual incident reviews
Load test: simulate 10k signals/sec to validate latency and scalability
metrics_to_track: Median enrichment latency and p99 latency
False positive rate measured by ops feedback tags
MTTD/MTTR on grouped incidents vs baseline
Customer-impact coverage by top-k scored incidents
